title: SUMIF with greater-than and less-than criteria
summary: Total only the lines at or above a target (or below a limit) using comparison criteria and a target stored in a cell.

blocks.text: The merchandising manager wants to know how much of the week's sales came from strong lines: those at or above a target of 100K. Weak lines under 60K need a separate look.
SUMIF can test numbers as well as words. You write the comparison in the criteria, for example ">=100", and SUMIF adds only the rows that pass.

items: Objective: use >, >=, < and <= criteria in SUMIF, including a target held in a cell.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: Put the comparison inside double quotes. If you leave out sum_range, SUMIF adds the cells in range itself, which suits "total of the big lines".
Only 150 is strictly above 120 (the 120 itself is not above 120), so the answer is 150K.

Suppose the target sits in cell F1. To use it, join the operator and the cell with &. The criteria becomes the text ">=100" when F1 holds 100. Writing ">=F1" inside the quotes would not work, because Excel would look for the letters F1.

items: The operators are > (greater than), >= (at least), < (less than) and <= (at most). > leaves out the exact value, >= includes it.
To add a different column, give sum_range: SUMIF(C2:C7,">=100",D2:D7) adds column D on the rows where column C is at least 100.
Comparison criteria only look at numbers. Text cells are never counted as bigger or smaller.

blocks.text: Use the sales in C2:C7 from Training (45, 80, 120, 60, 100, 150). Type whole numbers, for example 105.

items: Comparison criteria such as ">=100" and "<60" go in double quotes.
Join an operator to a cell with &, for example ">="&F1, to keep the target in one place.
>= includes the exact value and > leaves it out.
Give a sum_range to add a different column from the one you test.

blocks.text: Change the target in one cell and every total updates, so strong and weak lines can be reviewed in seconds.

items.prompt: Compared with ">=100", what does the criteria ">100" do to the line that sells exactly 100K?

options.label: It leaves that line out of the total

items.prompt: A target sits in F1. Which criteria uses it correctly?
